title: Fractions and decimals on the line

files.lesson.md: --- order: 11 unit: fractions node: AC9M7N04 n3 assumes: [AC9M4N04 n1, AC9M4N04 n2] uses: [AC9M7N07 n1] # ordering negatives (Comparing integers) title: Fractions and decimals on the line summary: Split each unit into equal parts and count from zero. A negative fraction or decimal counts to the left, so −1.5 sits halfway between −2 and −1. language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } connection: measuring-jug # data/connections/maths.yml hook: "A tide of −0.6 m, a share price down 1¼ dollars, a recipe with ¾ of a cup: numbers between the whole numbers, above and below zero." app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8164 url: http://127.0.0.1:8164/index.html readySelector: "#kmove-pt" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: line.yml#explain-pic, caption: "Quarters: $-1\\tfrac{1}{4}$ (A), $-\\tfrac{3}{4}$ (B) and $\\tfrac{1}{2}$ (C)." } explainClip: query: { code: "@line.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Split each unit, then count from zero" say: "Split each unit into equal parts, then count from zero." clip: - caption: { text: "Each unit is split into 4 quarters. P is 3 quarters right of 0.", say: "Each unit is split into four quarters. P is three quarters right of zero." } - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "Negative three quarters: 3 quarters left of 0.", say: "Negative three quarters is three quarters to the left of zero." } - click: Move P left - click: Move P left - click: Move P left - click: Move P left - click: Move P left - click: Move P left - wait: 400 - caption: { text: "−1 1/4: past −1, and one more quarter left.", say: "Negative one and a quarter: past negative one, and one more quarter left." } - click: Move P left - click: Move P left - expect: { selector: "#status", contains: "−1 1/4" } - wait: 1200 --- Between any two whole numbers on a number line there are fractions and decimals: $\tfrac{1}{2}$, $0.3$, $1\tfrac{3}{4}$. Below zero there are negative ones too: $-\tfrac{1}{2}$, $-0.3$, $-1\tfrac{3}{4}$. So where exactly does each one go, positive or negative, fraction, decimal or mixed numeral? ## Predict: where is −1.5? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a place for −1.5 before using the board tests whether they count the half towards zero or away from it." check: type: predict q: "Where does $-1.5$ go on a number line?" options: - "Halfway between $-2$ and $-1$" - "Halfway between $-1$ and $0$" - "Halfway between $1$ and $2$" - "Just to the left of $-15$" actual: "Halfway between −2 and −1. −1.5 is one and a half units below zero: count 1 unit left from 0, then half a unit further left." ``` Think of a temperature of $-1.5$ °C. Is it colder or warmer than $-1$ °C? ## Run: place it on the line ```step stage: run insight: "Dragging P to −1.5 and reading where it lands settles the prediction: the half is counted further from zero, to the left." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#run", height: 420 } check: { type: board, text: "Put $P$ at $-1.5$. Was your prediction right?", when: "x(P) = -1.5" } ``` Drag $P$ along the line, or pick it under **Move** and use the arrows. It lands on the halves. The board says where it is under the line. ## Investigate: count the parts ```step stage: investigate insight: "Split each unit into the denominator's number of parts and count from zero, to the left for a negative. Jo's mistake counts the 0.5 back towards zero." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Quick check: write $\\tfrac{3}{4}$ as a decimal." answer: "0.75" feedback: - ["0.34", "3/4 means 3 out of 4 equal parts, not 3 point 4. How many hundredths is a quarter?"] - ["3.4", "3/4 is less than 1."] explain: "One quarter is 0.25, so three quarters is 0.75." - check: type: question q: "Which is less, $-\\tfrac{3}{4}$ or $-\\tfrac{1}{4}$?" options: ["$-\\tfrac{3}{4}$", "$-\\tfrac{1}{4}$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Count quarters left from 0: which is further left?"] explain: "−3/4 is three quarters left of 0, further left than −1/4, so it is less." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#jo" text: "Jo places $-1.5$. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: negative-decimal-direction explain: "Line 4: −1.5 is 1.5 below zero, so the 0.5 is further below too. From −1, move half a unit left, to halfway between −2 and −1." ``` ### Quick check Converting fractions and decimals, from class. ### Placing −3/4 and −1 1/4 Here is how to place a negative fraction and a negative mixed numeral. ```worked -\tfrac{3}{4} :: The denominator is 4, so split each unit into 4 equal parts (quarters). \text{count 3 quarters left from } 0 :: Negative means left of zero. -\tfrac{3}{4} \text{ is between } -1 \text{ and } 0 :: It is 3 of the 4 quarters from 0 to $-1$. -1\tfrac{1}{4} = -1 - \tfrac{1}{4} :: A negative mixed numeral is a whole number and a part, both below zero. \text{count 1 unit left, then 1 quarter further left} :: The quarter is further from zero, not back towards it. -1\tfrac{1}{4} \text{ is between } -2 \text{ and } -1 :: Just past $-1$, a quarter of the way to $-2$. ``` Then: which is less, $-\tfrac{3}{4}$ or $-\tfrac{1}{4}$? ### Find the mistake Read Jo's working one line at a time. Which line moves the wrong way? ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a negative fraction, a negative mixed numeral, tenths, then a line that does not have zero in the middle, then the edge case of two names for one place." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#quarters", height: 420 } tasks: - starter: "line.yml#quarters" hint: "Each unit is split into 4. Count 1 quarter left from 0." check: { type: board, text: "Put $P$ at $-\\tfrac{1}{4}$.", when: "x(P) = -0.25", explain: "One quarter left of zero." } - starter: "line.yml#quarters" hint: ["Count 1 whole unit left from 0.", "Then 3 more quarters further left."] check: { type: board, text: "Put $P$ at $-1\\tfrac{3}{4}$.", when: "x(P) = -1.75", explain: "One unit left of zero, then three quarters further: a quarter short of −2." } - starter: "line.yml#tenths" hint: "This line is split into tenths. Count 6 tenths left from 0." check: { type: board, text: "Put $P$ at $-0.6$.", when: "x(P) = -0.6", explain: "Six tenths left of zero, a bit past halfway to −1." } - starter: "line.yml#offset" hint: "Zero is not in the middle of this line. Find it first." check: { type: board, text: "This line runs from $-2$ to $5$. Put $P$ at $-1\\tfrac{1}{2}$ and $Q$ at $2\\tfrac{1}{2}$.", when: "x(P) = -1.5 and x(Q) = 2.5", explain: "Find zero first, then count: P is 1½ left of 0, Q is 2½ right." } - check: type: question q: "Edge case: where do $-\\tfrac{2}{4}$ and $-0.5$ go?" options: ["At the same place: halfway between $-1$ and $0$", "$-\\tfrac{2}{4}$ is further left", "$-0.5$ is further left"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Simplify −2/4. Is it the same number as −0.5?", "−0.5 and −2/4 are both one half below zero."] explain: "−2/4 = −1/2 = −0.5: two names for one place on the line." ``` ### A negative fraction Each task changes one thing. First: quarters below zero. ### A negative mixed numeral ### Tenths ### Zero is not in the middle ### Two names, one place ## Practise: place and order ```step stage: practise insight: "Placing, ordering and comparing a mix of fractions and decimals; the review keeps integer ordering fresh." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Which list is in order from least to greatest?" options: ["$-1\\tfrac{1}{2},\\; -1.2,\\; -\\tfrac{3}{4},\\; 0.5$", "$-\\tfrac{3}{4},\\; -1.2,\\; -1\\tfrac{1}{2},\\; 0.5$", "$-1.2,\\; -1\\tfrac{1}{2},\\; -\\tfrac{3}{4},\\; 0.5$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Which of these is furthest left? −3/4 is closer to zero than −1.2.", "−1 1/2 is −1.5, further left than −1.2."] explain: "As decimals: −1.5, −1.2, −0.75, 0.5. Read left to right." - check: type: question q: "Which is greater, $-0.3$ or $-0.25$?" options: ["$-0.25$", "$-0.3$"] feedback: [null, "Write both in hundredths: −0.30 and −0.25. Which is further left?"] answer: 0 explain: "−0.25 is closer to zero, so it is greater: −0.3 < −0.25." - check: type: answer q: "What number is halfway between $-3$ and $-2$?" answer: "-2.5" feedback: - ["2.5", "Both ends are below zero, so the halfway point is too."] - ["-1.5", "That is halfway between −2 and −1. Look between −3 and −2."] explain: "−2.5, or −2 1/2." - check: type: question q: "Review: which is less, $-6$ or $-9$?" options: ["$-9$", "$-6$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Further left is less. Which is further left?"] explain: "−9 < −6: −9 is further left." ``` ### In order ### Which is greater? ### Halfway ### Review ## Make: always another number ```step stage: make insight: "Finding a number between two close numbers reverses the lesson: from the places back to a number, and shows there is always another one in between." try: { playground: board, starter: "line.yml#make", height: 420 } hint: ["This line is from −1 to 0, in steps of 0.05. Find −0.3 and −0.2.", "What number is halfway between them?"] check: { type: board, text: "Put $P$ at a number between $-0.3$ and $-0.2$.", when: "x(P) > -0.3 and x(P) < -0.2", explain: "−0.25 is halfway: between any two numbers on the line, there is always another." } ``` The line now shows only $-1$ to $0$, in twentieths. Find a number between $-0.3$ and $-0.2$. Stretch: find a number between $-\tfrac{1}{3}$ and $-\tfrac{1}{4}$. Can you always find another between any two? ## Make: a measuring jug on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A scale marked in quarters cannot show a third exactly; the paper task makes them put both on a common scale and compare the gaps." hint: ["Draw the jug from 1 to 2 and mark the quarters.", "Write 1½, 1⅔ and 1¾ all in twelfths."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A recipe needs $1\\tfrac{2}{3}$ cups of water. The jug is marked every quarter cup (the recipe is made up for the task). Which mark on the jug is nearest to $1\\tfrac{2}{3}$? Type it as a decimal, in cups." steps: - ["The marks near it are $1\\tfrac{1}{2} = 1.5$ and $1\\tfrac{3}{4} = 1.75$", "$1\\tfrac{2}{3}$ is about 1.67, between 1.5 and 1.75"] - ["In twelfths: $1\\tfrac{6}{12}$, $1\\tfrac{8}{12}$ and $1\\tfrac{9}{12}$", "twelfths are a common size for halves, thirds and quarters"] - ["$1\\tfrac{8}{12}$ is 1 twelfth below $1\\tfrac{9}{12}$ and 2 twelfths above $1\\tfrac{6}{12}$", "the nearer mark is the one with the smaller gap"] - ["The nearest mark is $1\\tfrac{3}{4}$, which is $1.75$ cups", "pour to the three-quarter mark; it is a little more than the recipe wants"] picks: - step: 3 q: "Why is $1.75$ nearer than $1.5$?" options: - "The gap to 1.75 is 1 twelfth and the gap to 1.5 is 2 twelfths, so 1.75 is closer" - "1.75 is a bigger number, so it is always the better choice" - "Thirds are always closer to the higher quarter" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "Bigger does not mean nearer. Compare the gaps on the line.", "It depends on the numbers. Here the gaps are 1 twelfth and 2 twelfths."] answer: "1.75" feedback: - ["1.5", "That is the mark below, and it is the farther one: 2 twelfths away, against 1 twelfth."] - ["1.67", "The jug has no mark there. Pick the nearest quarter."] criteria: - "I drew the jug as a number line with the quarter marks on it." - "I put 1⅔ between the two marks it sits between." - "I compared the two gaps, not just the size of the numbers." explain: "1⅔ is 1 8/12. The marks either side are 1 6/12 (2 twelfths away) and 1 9/12 (1 twelfth away), so the nearest mark is 1¾ = 1.75 cups." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The recipe is made up for the task, but the question is real: a jug marked in quarters cannot show a third exactly, so you place it between the marks and pick the nearer one. Draw the jug as a line, mark the quarters, then place the third. **Also used in** - **Kitchens.** Measuring cups and jugs are number lines, marked in halves, quarters or thirds. - **Thermometers and rulers.** Readings between the marks are placed by counting the parts, the same way, and below zero they count left. - **Fuel gauges.** An eighth of a tank is a place on a scale, not a count. ```teacher summary: Students place positive and negative fractions, decimals and mixed numerals on number lines split into halves, quarters and tenths, including lines without zero in the middle, and order them (AC9M7N04, node 3). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 6 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can place positive and negative fractions, decimals and mixed numerals on a number line. - I can explain why −1.5 is between −2 and −1, not between −1 and 0. - I can put a mixed set of fractions and decimals in order. struggle: "Negative fractions and decimals: counting the half towards zero instead of away from it, so that -1.5 lands between -1 and 0. Ask which way is colder, and count whole units left from zero first." before: > Do the Run board and the Make task yourself first. Students need Comparing integers (further left is less) and converting between fractions and decimals, which this lesson assumes was taught in class (node 2 of the descriptor); the Investigate step opens with a quick check of it. The one idea: split each unit into equal parts (the denominator) and count from zero, to the left for a negative. The common mistake is counting the part of a negative number back towards zero (−1.5 at −0.5); it is planted after the method, in Jo's working. On the board, a point's readout gives the fraction and the decimal (−1 1/4 (−1.25)). running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Students who chose 'between −1 and 0' are reading −1.5 as −1 then +0.5. Do not correct it yet." - "Run: ask students to say where −1.5 will land before they let go of P." - "Investigate: if many students miss the quick check, do the quarters (0.25, 0.5, 0.75) together first. Then model the worked example live: draw a line from −2 to 1, mark the quarters, and count aloud from zero for −3/4 and −1 1/4. Reveal the prepared lines afterwards to compare." - "Modify: before the line from −2 to 5, ask: where is zero on this line?" - "Practise: in the ordering question, students can write every number as a decimal first." - "Make: the board lands on −0.25; ask for other answers on paper (−0.21, −0.275). Then ask: is there a number between −0.3 and −0.25 too?" - "Paper: the measuring jug is worked in books; the page marks the nearest mark (1.75) and why it is nearer than 1.5. Books out, then look for the jug drawn as a line with the quarters marked before any comparing." stuck: - see: A student puts −1.5 between −1 and 0 (Jo's mistake). ask: Is −1.5 °C colder or warmer than −1 °C? fix: "Colder, so further left. Count 1 left, then half more left: −1.5 is further from zero than −1." - see: A student cannot place −3/4. ask: How many equal parts is each unit split into? Which way is negative? fix: "Count the quarters aloud from zero: −1/4, −2/4, −3/4." - see: A student thinks −0.3 is greater than −0.25 because 3 is less than 25. ask: Write both with two decimal places. Which is further left? fix: "−0.30 and −0.25: −0.30 is further from zero, so it is less." stretch: Find a number between −1/3 and −1/4. Then explain why there is always another number between any two. support: "Use the board for every question: the readout gives the fraction and the decimal. A strip of paper folded into quarters helps for the fractions." leads: > Next in Number: the four operations with positive fractions, decimals and percentages (AC9M7N06), then negative fractions and decimals, with the same moves as integers. Where it leads: plotting points with fractional coordinates, reading scales in science (thermometers, measuring cylinders), and the density of the rational numbers. exit: q: "Put in order from least to greatest: 0.4, −1 1/4, −0.8, −1/2." a: −1 1/4, −0.8, −1/2, 0.4. explain: > To place a fraction or decimal, **split each unit into equal parts and count from zero**. Quarters: split each unit into 4. Tenths: into 10. A negative number counts to the **left** of zero. $-\tfrac{3}{4}$ is three quarters left of 0. A negative mixed numeral or decimal is further left still: $-1.5$ is one unit left, then half a unit **further** left, halfway between $-2$ and $-1$. Once they are on the line, read from left to right to put them in order. ```

files.working.txt:
# Jo's working for the "find the mistake" task. Plain text: students click the wrong line, nothing runs.

# region: jo
Place −1.5 on the number line.
−1.5 is one and a half below zero.
Start at −1.
Move half a unit to the right, because 0.5 is positive.
So −1.5 is halfway between −1 and 0.
# endregion
